correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge6\) the injection of words into three-prefix, middle, and three-suffix blocks proves \(|C|\le|P||T|\,3^{n-6}\). The overlap-2 and overlap-3 restrictions imply disjoint A,B of pair ends and disjoint P,T triple ends. For each of \(3^9\) pair assignments, the integer optimum of allocating h common candidate triples is F(A,B); standard-library exhaustive verifier evaluates every assignment and an independent bitmask implementation confirms maximum 132. Construction has \(|P|=11\), \(|T|=12\), matching these bounds with disjoint two- and three-overlap sets. All quantifiers, end-index conventions, \(n\ge6\) boundary, and finite loops verified.

originality.rationale: The exact maximum at ternary base length six is not determined by the inspected interval-restricted-code papers. The length-scaling identity for \(n>6\) is explicitly credited to Stanovnik Proposition 3; the sharp 132 base value and attaining ternary extremal boundary sets require a new finite optimization. Yang--Ding give construction counts, Blackburn et al. the Cartesian prefix/suffix technique, and Stanovnik broad parameter bounds, none of which implies the exact \(q=3,t_1=2,t_2=3\) optimum without the missing finite calculation. Search failures are not novelty proofs; unindexed equivalent optimization remains a risk.
